P1.evidence: Frame delivered in full: 'just want to understand what's going on with your fitness right now. What are you looking to accomplish? What are some of the challenges that you've been dealing with? And then from there, if we can help with that, I can go into all the details about what we do.' Open question immediately after: 'in your opinion, what would you say is the biggest challenge that you're having with your fitness right now?' P1a partial — a KFS application existed and the rep acknowledged it while dismissing its usefulness, 'it was kind of, let's call it high level', without reading anything back. P1c partial — the agreement request is garbled in the transcript and no clean confirmation was obtained.

P2.evidence: Occupation was the best-run check anywhere in this batch — 'I thought I saw in your application that you're like a police officer right now, is that right?' followed by 'Were you more active when you were still a patrol officer?' and 'Are you still working crazy hours?', establishing patrol to desk, 9-to-5, and a seated commute. Energy was properly quantified with the strongest question of the batch: 'if you think back to before you went through your health scare, how would you rate your energy then compared to now?' produced 10-plus versus 5. Training status, results and diet all captured, and the gastritis was followed up twice including 'do you have any dietary restrictions of things that you can eat, maybe also due to your gastritis?' — genuinely better health probing than the rest of these calls. Against that, age, height and weight were all volunteered and never asked, sleep never came up on a call about halved energy levels, and P2d is the serious one: a right shoulder injury from two months ago that stopped him doing push-ups was disclosed in detail and drew not one follow-up question — not how long, not whether it resolved, not whether anyone looked at it.

P3.evidence: Ran properly. 'Are there any specific parts of your fitness that you're looking to improve right now? Maybe weight, like fat, muscle, mobility, endurance, performance?' opened it; 'Any particular reason why you're wanting to build up the muscle again?' and 'what caused you to start again?' drove it, producing both the SWAT tryout he lost and the deeper answer — 'I feel like I'm not myself, like what I used to be.' The energy-scaling question doubled as the what-does-it-do-for-you move and landed hard. The reflect-back was clean and confirmed: 'sounds like you're getting back your confidence, just being back in the shape you were, getting more energy and mobility, not feeling aches and pains' — 'Yeah, for sure.' The gap is P3f: the unborn child appeared five separate times and was only ever raised as a leading prompt ('maybe your unborn child?'), never as an open question about who this affects, and never built into a stake.

P4.evidence: Past attempts asked directly — 'was there ever a point where you worked with an online fitness coach in the past?' — producing in-person trainers, his baseball trainers and, crucially, a six-month online one-to-one nutrition programme. The garage-gym restart was properly opened up with 'even with the at-home gym, it's still doing those workouts, it's not...', which produced the whole ego-lifting story and the shoulder injury that ended it. What did not run: why it did not stick was never asked, the prospect supplied the time-cost blocker himself ('my biggest thing, Ben, is just the consumption of time'), and P4f was never attempted. That last one matters here — he already pays for remote one-to-one coaching with a nutritionist in New Zealand and it worked, which is both the strongest available proof that the model suits him and the exact thread that would have justified the price.

P5.evidence: Never ran, on the call in this batch with the richest material for it. A first child arriving on Christmas Day, energy halved, a job that may put him back on the street, and a childhood ambition he had just missed because his shoulder gave out. Not one of those was turned into a cost of another six months of nothing. No two-year question, no willingness-to-settle, no line in the sand. When the wife and the money surfaced at the end there was nothing behind them.

P6.evidence: P6a ran in the right place and in the right order — 'right now, do you feel like you're ready to start going through the plan, getting in there, working out again, and starting to make these changes?' at 00:33:20, twenty minutes before the price, answered 'I'm ready, definitely ready.' That is the correct sequencing and it is worth crediting. But the yes was explicitly conditional — 'I think it all depends on what that looks like as far as schedule-wise' — and was treated as clean. P6b was never asked, and it is the omission that decided the call: 'if you had everything you needed, is there any reason you wouldn't go all in' would have surfaced the wife and the money at minute 33 instead of minute 80, leaving fifty minutes to work with them.

P11.evidence: No close attempted. No payment link was sent, no deposit offered, no onboarding booked and no follow-up call scheduled. The rep texted his phone number so the prospect could initiate contact later. Nothing in the phase was reachable.

objection_plays.detail: 'Discuss with my wife. That's a principle that I have.' None of the six moves ran. No money-aside belief check, no 'when you talk to her, what obstacles might come up', no 'is there any reason she would not want you stronger', no separation of genuine input from permission, and no refundable deposit. The unrun move that mattered most was obvious on this call: his wife is pregnant with their first child, he has stated the reason for training is to be healthy enough to chase that child, and nobody asked whether she would object to that. The rep's actual response was to invent a 30-day arrangement, which does not address the objection at all — it defers it.

Money was raised clearly — 'can I put this on a credit card? Or are we going to work out payment plans and maybe cut it between $3,000, $3,000?' — and the prospect volunteered his own financial picture unprompted ('I would think that I would have the money to do it, even if I have to put it on a credit card'). The rep listed options: two payments of $3,000, three of $2,000, or monthly at roughly an extra $200. Nothing else ran — no isolation question, no HOW-not-SHOULD reframe, none of the financial-picture questions, and critically no plan was actually fixed and no link sent, so the prospect left with three unstructured possibilities rather than one number to take to his wife.

'I'm going to sit on this for tonight' and 'hopefully I can have some time to just think about it.' The rep asked 'where's your head at?', which is a reasonable opener, and then ran none of the play. No 'what's actually coming up that's preventing you from getting started', no 'thinking isn't the problem, deciding is', and no version of 'the man you want to be — how does he decide right now', which was available given he had just described missing the SWAT tryout he had wanted since childhood.

A structural objection with no scripted play, raised four separate times: he wants Trevor's professional assessment of his body and goals in order to choose between six and twelve months, and that assessment only happens after payment. 'I definitely want to hear from him personally... let me know what you think from the beginning.' The rep's answer was that he could raise it on the onboarding call, which is after the money. The sequence blocks the prospect's own stated decision process and nothing in the script addresses it.

A trust-and-proof question aimed at the rep personally: 'Do you believe in this program, and have you seen it firsthand? I know you work alongside with Trevor, but would you recommend it and why?' Answered with a detailed personal testimonial about mobility work, joint clicking and energy. Effective in the moment; the accuracy of that testimonial is logged separately against the internal record.
No timing objection — if anything the baby's arrival is being used as a reason to start now.
No fear about the programme working; his stated concern was about hurting himself again, which the offer directly answers.

notes: An 84-minute call with a genuinely strong discovery — the occupation, energy and goals work is the best in this batch — that then improvised every commercial answer it gave. A three-month tier at $4,000, a payment plan implying $7,200, 'we don't have a prorated rate' reversed four minutes later, and a 30-day entry arrangement invented on the spot with a promise to tell the team. None of it is written down and all of it is now being repeated to his wife. Two coaching actions. First, run P6b before the price: this prospect gave a conditional yes at minute 33 and the wife and the money did not surface until minute 80. Second, and more urgent than any of it, he disclosed a shoulder injury two months old that stopped him doing push-ups and it drew no question at all.
